basis: Directives Part 1, Working Draft 0.2, D1-030, D1-031, D1-032 and D1-074; archived source publications/archive/0.2/governance/directives_part_1.tex
assessment_boundary: Four-count arithmetic only. N, Y, D and A are nonnegative integer counts, excluding booleans, with Y+D+A <= N. N=0 is a valid numerical input but cannot satisfy the substantive minimum. All attempted submissions are assumed valid in this four-count fixture; this assumption does not specify a voting-service input contract or permit nonresponse to absorb invalid attempts. Authored expected outcomes are not an execution record. No appointment, ballot, independent verification, timing, consensus or adoption has occurred.

cases.notes: One nonresponse; the remaining dissent still needs reasoned handling.
Unanimity among three respondents does not supply quorum for six eligible persons.
Abstentions supply returned-ballot quorum but not substantive participation.
Original hypothetical roster and tally before a later recusal.
Hypothetical recusal changes the result. The numerical pass cannot amend the original outcome; a new ballot is required.
Smallest substantive electorate allowed by the numerical rule; breadth and independence remain separate questions.
Two unanimous eligible persons cannot meet the substantive minimum.
Ceilings matter for both a seven-person roster and four substantive returns.
Same quorum as B07; only the substantive split changes.
Exact two-thirds substantive support with rounded-up returned-ballot quorum.
Three of five substantive votes falls short despite six returns.
The bare inequality Y>=0 is true, but zero substantive votes decisively fails the combined rule.
Zero is a valid mathematical count domain boundary, not evidence of a constituted electorate.
Four counted persons exceed the eligible roster. Reject the count input; do not call it a valid failed ballot.
Negative counts are outside the fixture domain.
Fractional persons are outside the fixture domain.
This fixture does not silently coerce a numeric string to a count.
A Boolean is not an integer count in this fixture, even in a programming language that subclasses integers.
